case.name: In re AT&T Inc. Customer Data Security Breach Litigation
case.court: US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, Dallas Division
case.special_master: Royal Furgeson, a retired US District Judge

admin_update.text: Payments have not been issued yet. Payments cannot be made until the Settlement becomes "effective." That happens only after the time to appeal has ended and any post-judgment motions or appeals are resolved. Payments are not expected to be issued in 2026.

incidents.label: AT&T 1
incidents.data: some combination of names, addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, account passcodes, billing account numbers and Social Security numbers
incidents.defendants: AT&T Inc., AT&T Mobility LLC, AT&T Corporation and DirecTV, LLC

incidents.label: AT&T 2
incidents.data: telephone numbers of current and former customers, the telephone numbers they interacted with, counts of those interactions, aggregate call durations for a day or month and, for a small subset, cell site identification numbers
incidents.not_included: text content, customer names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth or other personal or financial information
incidents.defendants: AT&T Mobility LLC, AT&T Services, Inc. and Cricket Wireless LLC

benefits.estimates_source: Kroll Omnibus Declaration (ECF No. 517) paragraph 40, as quoted in the final approval order

estimates.who: AT&T 1 members whose Social Security number was exposed
AT&T 1 members whose Social Security number was not exposed

timeline.what: The AT&T 1 data set is on the dark web by this date, according to the complaint.
The Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation sends the AT&T 1 suits to Dallas as MDL No. 3114.
AT&T announces the second incident, the call records taken from its Snowflake workspace (AT&T 2).
The Snowflake suits, AT&T 2 among them, are sent to Judge Brian Morris in Montana.
Three days of mediation begin. Both cases reach agreements in principle.
One settlement agreement for both incidents is signed and filed in Dallas.
Judge Ada E. Brown grants preliminary approval.
Last day to opt out or object.
The case is reassigned to Senior Judge Sidney A. Fitzwater after Judge Brown recuses.
Last day to answer a notice of deficient claim.
Final approval granted, with fees, costs and service awards.
The administrator posts that payments are not expected in 2026.
